In his speech, he defended Orbán’s “Greater Hungary” map in his office, mentioned the Beneš Decrees, and referred to the Austro-Hungarian Empire as a positive example. He also talked about creating a “V8” alliance of Central European countries, maintaining zero immigration, and argued that Marine Le Pen’s party in France is not far-right, but rather patriotic—like people such as himself.
I think there are currently crisis talks among EU leaders: we might grabbed a tiger by the tail.
Listen carefully to the second part of his three-hour press conference, where he answers questions.
